lessonTitle: The General Survey: First Impressions Count
description: What you notice in the first thirty seconds — appearance, gait, breathing and colour.
A systematic full examination — the order, the techniques and the findings worth noting.
Stethoscope, sphygmomanometer, thermometer and penlight — using each one properly.
Building your internal library of normal so that the abnormal jumps out at you.

lessonTitle: Which Finding Should You Report Immediately?
description: Practising the escalation decisions that separate safe students from risky ones.
Verbal, non-verbal and written — the three channels every nurse must master.
Pain, fear, language, noise and hierarchy — the obstacles between you and understanding.
The specific techniques — open questions, silence, reflection — that turn conversation into therapy.

lessonTitle: Documentation in Practice: Writing That Protects
description: Clear, legal, honest notes — writing for the patient, the team and the record.
Giving and receiving report safely — structure, brevity and no important gaps.
Warm but boundaried — caring without becoming the patient's friend or their problem.
Looking honestly at how you come across — the fastest way to improve it.
